title: Rust: Module System
description: Organize code using Rust's module system with visibility and paths.

steps.title: Simple Module
steps.description: Define a module `math` inline with `mod math { ... }` containing an `add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32` function. Call `math::add(3, 4)` and print the result.
hints: `mod math { pub fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b } }`
Functions are private by default — use `pub` to make them accessible.

verification.failureMessage: Define a math module with add function and print 3+4=7.

steps.title: Nested Modules
steps.description: Create nested modules: `mod shapes { pub mod circle { pub fn area(r: f64) -> f64 { 3.14159 * r * r } }; pub mod rect { pub fn area(w: f64, h: f64) -> f64 { w * h } } }`. Print area of circle(5) and rect(3,4).
hints: Each module needs `pub` on the module and the function.

verification.failureMessage: Call area functions in nested modules and print results.

steps.title: use Keyword
steps.description: Use `use` to bring modules into scope: `use shapes::circle::area as circle_area`. Then call `circle_area(5.0)` directly. Print the result.
hints: `use shapes::circle::area;` brings the function into scope.
`as` creates an alias: `use shapes::rect::area as rect_area;`.
Without `use`, you must use full paths.

verification.failureMessage: Import circle area function with use and call it.

steps.title: Visibility (pub(crate))
steps.description: Create a module with different visibility levels: `pub` (public), `pub(crate)` (crate-wide), no pub (private). Demonstrate that private items can't be accessed from outside.
hints: `pub(crate) fn crate_fn() {}` accessible within the crate.
Private: only accessible within the module and submodules.

verification.failureMessage: Show the difference between pub, pub(crate), and private.

steps.title: Module with Struct
steps.description: Create a module `user` with a struct `User { pub name: String, pub age: i32, id: String }`. The `id` field is private. Implement a `new` constructor. Print user's name and age.
hints: `pub struct User { pub name: String, pub age: i32, id: String }`
`impl User { pub fn new(name: &str, age: i32) -> Self { Self { name: name.into(), age, id: uuid() } } }`
Accessible fields: name and age. Private: id.

verification.failureMessage: Create a User struct in a module and print its public fields.
